phenomenon: an unrelated standalone meaning must not veto a paradigm the same surface form supports
notes: The prompt's HOMOGRAPHY DOES NOT BLOCK A PARADIGM rule, tested twice in one item. Standalone L is 'the left face' and standalone V is 'the vertical seam', yet inside Ld/Lb the L is LAMP and inside Vd/Vb the V is VENT. Ld/Lb is the decisive minimal pair: same frame, corresponding meaning contrast. The standalone entries stay lexical -- they are separate codebook symbols, not occurrences inside a code -- while the bound occurrences are analyzed. A judge that lets the whole-code homograph veto the DEVICE class will leave the whole family lexical and fail recall here.
